_comment: Reviewed prose stored as data — tier 2 of the three-tier rule in sources/scope.md ('No free-generated text on the site'). Each block carries a status: every tier-2 text passes through one review before flipping to 'approved', with the review date recorded in 'reviewed'; 'final' marks the masthead pair George signed off as-is. Slots in {braces} are filled at build time from gate-checked objects — never hardcoded here. The site-wide blocks resolve their slots against the site summary object (data/summaries/site.json) in web/lib/sitetext.ts; 'ego_notes' resolves its slots against the computed ego view in sources/build_ego_views.py, which bakes the rendered sentence into data/graph/ego/<file>.json.

masthead.tagline: EU legislation, decoded into data: each measure, every sector it affects, every supply chain it reaches.
masthead.subline: The intelligence layer between EU legislation and the real economy.

perimeter.template: PolicyFocus decodes EU legislation into data. Each act is read provision by provision into individual measures: obligations, prohibitions, incentives, and rights, every one carrying the verbatim source text and a link to the official version. Measures are mapped to sectors in two ways: sectors an act names directly, and sectors it reaches through supply chains, regulatory dependencies, or procurement channels, with supply-chain reach computed from Eurostat input-output data. The measures are then aggregated per sector, so each sector page shows its full position across all legislation on the platform: what binds it directly, what reaches it indirectly, and through which channel. The platform currently holds {measures_count} measures from {acts_count} legislative acts across {sectors_count} sectors, and it grows as new legislation is adopted. Every act's verification status is stated on the coverage page. The platform does not cover national implementing measures or guidance documents, and nothing on this site is legal advice.

files.ppwr: The packaging regulation's classifications are from a preliminary reading and have not yet been independently confirmed.

coverage_line.template: {acts_count} acts decoded so far; the platform grows as new legislation is adopted.

ego_notes._comment: One note per register file whose measures name and reach no sector at all. A note is REQUIRED for such a file: build_ego_views.py fails rather than composing one, because the sentence has to say what a missing sector ring means, and only a person can decide that. Slots are computed by the builder from the view it has just built — {measure_count} is the file's own measure count, {act_count} the number of distinct acts its spokes point at. Both are filled the same way; nothing in the sentence is a typed-in number.

files.omnibus: None of the omnibus's {measure_count} measures names a specific sector. The act applies horizontally, to companies across the whole economy based on size and activity. Zero named sectors means no sector-specific provisions, not zero impact. Every connection shown is one of the {act_count} acts its measures amend, cite or depend on.

record_templates._comment: One template family per legislative-event shape. Slots in {braces} are computed by sources/build_records.py from the register and the manifest and filled at build time; a slot the builder cannot compute fails the build rather than rendering empty, and a record whose event fits no family here fails the build rather than being composed. Written in display vocabulary from the start, per the display-vocabulary ruling in sources/scope.md: measures and sectors, never rows or register. STATUS IS DRAFT: build_records.py will build these records and warn, and the page layer must refuse to render a family whose status is not 'approved'. George flips the status after reading the three backfilled records.

new_act_ingested.headline: {act_name}: {measure_count} measures now on the platform, naming {named_count} sectors
new_act_ingested.body: {act_name} is now on the platform. Its {measure_count} measures have been read one provision at a time. The act names {named_count} sectors in its own text — most often {top_sector}, on {top_sector_named_count} measures — and reaches {reached_count} more through supply chains, dependencies on other acts, or procurement.

amendment.headline: {act_name} amended: {measure_count} measures change
amendment.body: {act_name} has been amended. {measure_count} measures change, affecting {named_count} sectors named in the act's own text and {reached_count} more reached through supply chains, dependencies on other acts, or procurement. Where the wording of the earlier rule could be sourced, each measure below shows what it said before and what it says now.

delegated_act.headline: {act_name}: {measure_count} measures set by a delegated act
delegated_act.body: A delegated act has landed under {act_name}. It settles {measure_count} measures that the parent act left to be filled in later, affecting {named_count} sectors named in the act's own text and {reached_count} more reached through supply chains, dependencies on other acts, or procurement.

status_change.headline: {act_name} moves from proposal to adopted law
status_change.body: {act_name} is no longer a proposal. Its {measure_count} measures are adopted law, binding {named_count} sectors named in the act's own text and reaching {reached_count} more through supply chains, dependencies on other acts, or procurement.

status_notes._comment: Appended to every record body, chosen by the legal standing of the act the record is about — the same STATUS_RULE the findings gate applies. A record about a proposal has to say so on its own face: the record is permanent and will outlive the proposal.
status_notes.adopted: This act is adopted. It is law, not a proposal.
status_notes.proposed: This is a Commission proposal, {com}, under procedure {procedure}. It is not law yet, and it can change before it is.
status_notes.mixed: The proposal {com}, under procedure {procedure}, would change an act already in force. What it adds is not law yet; the act it changes is.
